open_release.rationale: The paper and README frame synthetic EHR as a way to give researchers access without identifiable patient data.

quotes.text: Synthetic Electronic Health Records (EHR) have emerged as a pivotal tool in advancing healthcare applications and machine learning models, particularly for researchers without direct access to healthcare data.
implementing advanced privacy-preserving techniques to ensure generated data contains no identifiable information

pipeline_testing.rationale: OMOP compatibility is for dissemination of realistic data, not for exercising software without a realism claim.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The paper defines and evaluates ML utility, requiring models trained on synthetic data to match those trained on real data.

statistical_replication.rationale: The paper and README evaluate marginal distributions and co-occurrence fidelity against the source data.

quotes.text: The synthetic data maintains statistical fidelity to real patient populations without containing identifiable information, and outputs are fully compatible with the OMOP Common Data Model.

causal_inference.rationale: Counterfactual reasoning is only listed as a general GPT application; the work itself focuses on synthetic generation without causal claims.

education.rationale: No teaching or tutorial framing for the synthetic data appears in the sources.

benchmarking.rationale: The baselines in the paper are the authors' own model variants, and CEHR-GPT is not positioned as a benchmark for others.

imbalance_correction.rationale: No class-imbalance or minority-class framing appears in the sources.
